scope: LONGHORN-48 V2 external S3/TLS full/incremental fixture and independent restore integration; not project PASS
conclusions: Off-cluster S3 objects survive local-volume loss; cluster-local TLS passthrough is a temporary lab transport, so its endpoint is not a production disaster-independent path.
Secret in the installation namespace provides AWS_ENDPOINTS, AWS_CERT PEM CA chain and VIRTUAL_HOSTED_STYLE; fixture uses path style, verifies CA/host and changes no customer defaults.

Full backup uploads all data blocks and overwrites existing ones; incremental transfers changed blocks, so upstream GA does not prove this project requested the intended mode or can recover either time boundary.

Validate actual backup configuration and every referenced object, then independent restored PVC/PV/Volume and source write isolation through existing config+kubecli integration; target readiness alone is insufficient.
Backup lifecycle remains Longhorn-owned: no backend retention/deletion policy. Cleanup restores original target references only after native backup and consumer cleanup.

Official restore CR sample uses V1; this gate explicitly uses V2 StorageClass through CSI, backed by existing snapshot/CSI pinned source research; no claim for encrypted recovery, scheduling, SystemRestore or DR.

RFC 5280 4.2.1.1/2/3 require leaf AuthorityKeyIdentifier, CA SubjectKeyIdentifier and CA KeyUsage; Python 3.13+ strict SSL verification exposes missing fixture extensions. Use a backup-only compliant chain, retaining CA/host verification and independently qualified gRPC identities.
BackupTarget availability comes from ListSystemBackup using Secret-derived credentials; it is distinct from per-volume object/readback and restore proof.

backupstore saveBlock compresses data before getTransferDataSize, then tracks newly uploaded or overwritten existing content-addressed objects. Reported transfer byte counts are compressed streams, not logical volume or application sizes.
